tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed its first weekly-test start; it started second after ~8 s cranking with batteries at 22.8 V at rest, then achieved rated pressure. Partner FW-8101 later delivered 9.2 barg versus 11 barg design; flow was unmeasured.
tickets.recommended_action: Load-test batteries and inspect starting system; correct per fire-protection engineer, then prove first-attempt start and rated flow/pressure. Check impairment deviation record. Retest first-start and rated delivery. Test FW-8101 rated flow and pressure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Required first-attempt starting failed during an actual weekly function test. The later start and normal running preserve delivery evidence but do not undo the demonstrated starting-function loss.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start removes one safety-critical firewater pump from dependable demand service. The N+1 partner cannot be credited as fully capable because its later test showed 9.2 barg versus 11 barg design and no measured flow, leaving severe fire-protection exposure without proving total firewater loss.

tickets.recommended_action: Expand CUI inspection at the low-point drain; integrity engineer to assess and dispose, repair as approved, then verify fitness for full pressure. Check local exposure and escalation Map wall loss beyond the windows

tickets.summary: Main-hoist rope has 6 broken wires per lay versus a 10-wire discard limit at the maximum-radius drum section; poor lubrication may accelerate deterioration.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect the full hoist rope, lubricate the deficient section, obtain lifting-authority disposition, and verify the discard criterion. Check lift loads and personnel exposure. Inspect full rope and compare wire counts. Obtain lifting-authority disposition.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Six broken wires and poor lubrication establish limited degradation, but the measured count retains margin to the 10-wire discard criterion and no failed hoisting function is reported.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the sole main-deck crane's hoisting function could create serious lifting exposure and stop supply-boat offloads, producing a logistics problem within days; no redundant crane is identified.

tickets.summary: P-3305 inhibitor injection was intermittent for about 10 days after three low-pressure trips this month; diaphragm failure is suspected, with downstream corrosion possible within weeks.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect diaphragm/trip; repair per findings. Integrity engineer to disposition and verify required injection pressure/flow. Assess downstream corrosion exposure. Check impairment deviation record. Inspect diaphragm and trip cause. Verify continuous inhibitor injection.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The required injection function has already been interrupted three times this month and remained intermittent for around ten days. The suspected diaphragm cause is unconfirmed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the sole corrosion-inhibitor pump can leave downstream carbon steel without inhibition; corrosion starts within weeks and creates a delayed integrity consequence, although the eventual exposure magnitude is not established.

tickets.summary: Loose, wind-flapping cladding on K-3401 second-stage discharge line is expected to become a dropped object; process function is unaffected, but personnel exposure is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Barricade exposure area; inspect and secure or replace cladding under responsible engineer disposition; verify retention. Check drop zone and personnel exposure. Inspect cladding retention.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Active wind movement and the explicit expectation of a dropped object indicate advanced degradation and strong progression toward loss of cladding retention, without confirmed detachment.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Detached cladding is a credible dropped-object hazard with potential for severe personnel injury; the actual consequence depends on drop height and exposure beneath the line.
